figures.alt: Equipment for the preparation of ethyl ethanoate
figures.caption: The preparation of ethyl ethanoate

specPoints.text: know that ethyl ethanoate is the ester produced when ethanol and ethanoic acid react in the presence of an acid catalyst
practical: prepare a sample of an ester such as ethyl ethanoate

primer.text: From Esters you already know ethyl ethanoate as the ester of ethanol and ethanoic acid. This note turns the recipe into a real experiment: gentle heating with the acid catalyst, distilling the ester out as it forms, and washing the sample clean of everything that travelled with it.

lessons.title: Aim and method: gentle heat and a quick exit
lessons.opening: The practical makes a small sample of ethyl ethanoate from its two parents and the acid catalyst. Ethanol is flammable, so the heating stays gentle: a water bath or electric heater instead of a flame, and the ester is distilled off the moment it forms.
keyPoints: The aim is to make a small sample of ethyl ethanoate.
Ethanoic acid, ethanol and concentrated sulfuric acid are heated gently together.
A water bath or electric heater replaces a Bunsen flame because ethanol is flammable.
The ester is distilled off as soon as it forms and collected by condensation.
Distilling the ester away stops the reverse reaction re-forming the reactants.

low.restatement: Ethanoic acid, ethanol and concentrated sulfuric acid are warmed gently together, with no naked flame because ethanol is flammable. The ester boils off first and is collected as it condenses in a separate beaker.
low.analogy: The setup is a gentle spa rather than a furnace: warm water does the heating, and the ester is ushered out the moment it appears.
low.examPointer: Name the safety reason for the water bath; the flammability of ethanol is the expected answer.

medium.restatement: A gentle heat from a water bath or electric heater warms ethanoic acid, ethanol and concentrated sulfuric acid together. The ester, being volatile with a low boiling point, leaves the mixture first and is distilled off at once, so the reverse reaction cannot push it back into reactants.
medium.analogy: Distilling the ester away is like serving food the second it is plated: nothing sits around long enough to be sent back to the kitchen.
medium.examPointer: Link low boiling points to leaving first, and removal to preventing the reverse reaction; both ideas carry marks.

check.stem: Which three substances are heated together in the flask?

options.text: Ethanoic acid, ethanol and concentrated sulfuric acid
options.explanation: The two parents plus the acid catalyst are the charged mixture.
Water is the product to be avoided, not an ingredient of the charge.

options.text: Ethanol, sodium carbonate and calcium chloride
options.explanation: Those two solutions belong to the purification stage afterwards.
Magnesium belongs to acid-metal reactions, not to this ester practical.

check.stem: Why is a Bunsen burner not used for the heating?

options.text: Ethanol is flammable, so a naked flame is unsafe
options.explanation: A water bath or electric heater gives gentle heat without ignition risk.

options.text: The ester would burn away to nothing
options.explanation: The concern is igniting the ethanol vapour, not destroying the product.

options.text: The catalyst only works when cold
options.explanation: The method explicitly heats the mixture; only the heat source changes.

options.text: Bunsen flames are banned in all school practicals
options.explanation: Flames are used where safe; here the flammable ethanol rules one out.

check.stem: Why is the ester distilled off as soon as it forms?

options.text: Removing it stops the reverse reaction turning it back into reactants
options.explanation: Taking the product away shifts the reaction in its favour and protects the yield.

options.text: To make its smell stronger in the sample
options.explanation: The distillation protects the yield; the smell is only a later check.

options.text: To save heating time and electricity
options.explanation: Economy is not the chemical reason; the reverse reaction is.

options.text: To keep the ester dissolved in the acid
options.explanation: The opposite is true: the method removes it from the mixture entirely.

check.stem: Why do esters leave the reaction mixture before the other liquids?

options.text: Their low boiling points make them the first to evaporate
options.explanation: Volatility puts the ester at the front of the queue when the mixture warms.

options.text: They are the heaviest liquids present
options.explanation: Low boiling points, not heavy mass, decide who leaves first.

options.text: They are solids that melt early
options.explanation: Esters here are oily liquids from the start.
Water is the by-product and plays no part in the exit order.

check.stem: How is the distilled ester collected?

options.text: In a separate beaker by condensation
options.explanation: The vapour cools back to liquid and gathers in its own vessel.
Filtration is for solids, and the ester arrives as a liquid.
The point of distilling off is to leave the flask behind.
No freezing stage exists in this method.

lessons.title: Result: washing the sample clean
lessons.opening: The collected distillate is more than ester: acids and ethanol travel over with it. Washing follows, first with sodium carbonate solution until the fizzing stops, then with calcium chloride solution to catch the ethanol, leaving the sweet ester behind.
keyPoints: Smelling the distillate confirms whether an ester has formed.
Small amounts of ethanoic acid, sulfuric acid and ethanol come over with the ester.
Sodium carbonate solution removes the acidic impurities until the mixture stops fizzing.
The fizzing ends when no further carbon dioxide escapes.
Calcium chloride solution removes the leftover ethanol from the sample.

low.restatement: Smell the distillate for the sweet ester. Sodium carbonate washing removes the acids until fizzing stops, and calcium chloride washing removes the leftover ethanol.
low.analogy: The washes are a bouncer pair: the carbonate escorts out the acids, the chloride escorts out the ethanol, and only the ester stays at the party.
low.examPointer: Match each wash to what it removes; the pairing is a standard practical question.

medium.restatement: The raw distillate carries small quantities of ethanoic acid, sulfuric acid and ethanol alongside the ester. Sodium carbonate is added until no further carbon dioxide escapes, showing the acids are gone, and calcium chloride solution then strips out the ethanol.
medium.analogy: Purifying runs like a two-question quiz: does it still fizz, and has the ethanol gone; each wash answers one question before the sample is clean.
medium.examPointer: Quote the fizzing test as evidence the acidic impurities have gone; the observation carries the mark.

check.stem: How is the product checked before any washing begins?

options.explanation: The sweet smell of the ester is the quick qualitative check the method names.
Laboratory chemicals are never tasted, whatever they smell like.

options.text: By burning a little of it
options.explanation: Igniting a flammable distillate is not part of this method.
Mass alone cannot confirm which substances are present.

check.stem: Why is sodium carbonate solution added to the distillate?

options.explanation: The carbonate neutralises both acids until none remain to fizz.

options.text: To add flavour to the ester
options.explanation: Flavouring happens in food factories, not in this purification.
Drying agents are different substances; the carbonate targets acids.
The reaction is already over; the carbonate works on impurities.

check.stem: What is the fizzing during the sodium carbonate wash?

options.text: Carbon dioxide released as the carbonate meets the acids
options.explanation: Carbonate plus acid always releases the gas, and the fizzing shows it leaving.
No hydrogen is produced by this neutralisation.
Oxygen is not generated in an acid-carbonate reaction.
The distillate is already liquid; the bubbles are gas from the neutralisation.

check.stem: What does the calcium chloride solution remove?

options.explanation: Calcium chloride is the named remover of ethanol from the sample.
The acids were already removed by the sodium carbonate wash.
Water removal is not the stated job of this solution here.
The product is what the washing is protecting, not removing.

check.stem: Which contaminants can still be present in the raw distillate before washing?

options.text: Ethanoic acid, sulfuric acid and ethanol
options.explanation: All three travel over with the volatile ester during the distillation.
The method names three specific travellers, not just water.
Neither metal nor its gas plays any part in this practical.
No chloride salts are involved before the washing stage.

glossary.definition: Boiling off and collecting a component; the ester is distilled off as soon as it forms.
Vapour turning back to liquid as it cools; the distillate is collected this way in a beaker.
Boiling or evaporating readily; esters are volatile, so they leave the reaction mixture first.
Catches fire easily; ethanol is flammable, so no Bunsen flame is used for heating.
An unwanted substance mixed with the product, here the two acids and leftover ethanol.

workedExample.prompt: Describe the preparation of a sample of ethyl ethanoate from ethanol and ethanoic acid, including the heating choice, why the ester is distilled off as soon as it forms, and how the distillate is purified.
steps: Gently heat ethanoic acid, ethanol and concentrated sulfuric acid (the acid catalyst) using a water bath or electric heater — no Bunsen flame, because ethanol is flammable.
Distil the ester off as soon as it forms: esters are volatile with low boiling points, so they evaporate first, and removing them prevents the reverse reaction from re-forming the reactants.
Collect the condensate in a separate beaker and smell it to confirm the sweet ester has been produced.

Wash the distillate with sodium carbonate solution until the fizzing stops (this removes the ethanoic and sulfuric acid impurities), then with calcium chloride solution to remove the leftover ethanol.
workedExample.finalAnswer: Water-bath heating (ethanol is flammable); distil off at once (volatile — blocks the reverse reaction); wash with sodium carbonate solution, then calcium chloride solution.
